newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng Index may find 14,000 hard to crack.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index may find 14,000 hard to crack.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks have staged a staggering rally over recent sessions, bringing the Hang Seng Index's record high within sights again, but analysts said 14,000 points may prove tough to crack in the near-term.
"Recently there has been a shift in sentiment and people are a lot more optimistic about the interest rate outlook," Percy Au-Young, DBS Securities director of research, said on Tuesday.
"A lot of people are now saying that the market can go through 14,000 but I do not expect the market to break 14,000. At that level the market is getting quite expensive," he said.
The Hang Seng Index on Tuesday breached 13,600 points for the first time since late February.

The blue chip index rose to an intra-day high of 13,679.92 points before closing at 13,579.34, up 180.00 points or 1.34 percent. The rise brought the cumulative gains over the past five sessions to 978.92 points, or 7.77 percent.
Since the Hang Seng hit a record high of 14,004.93 points on January 16 the market has been plagued by fears of higher interest rates and a correction in real estate prices.
"Investors' expectations this week have changed," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"People think there is less likelihood of a May 20 interest rate hike. Purely on a laggard basis they have recognised that (property stocks) are looking fairly attractive," he said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting body is due to meet on May 20 to deliberate on interest rates.
Analysts said recent U.S. economic data, a decline in the U.S. long bond yield below seven percent, and an agreement to balance the U.S. budget had bolstered sentiment on the interest rate front.
But with the Fed meeting still hanging over the market, the market could suffer some near-term profit-taking, they said.

"There is still a chance for an interest rate hike. Even if there is not an interest rate hike in the short term....that will cap the upside," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.

Analysts also said that although some investors were expecting a recovery in real estate prices following a slump of some 10 percent since late March, they may be a little too hasty in predicting a pick-up.
"It will probably take more time to consolidate before moving up," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
Property stocks lost some of their recent momentum by Tuesday's close with Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd finishing lower.
"Today I see some selling pressure in the property sector. I expect the market might be entering some consolidation," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
"It will probably stay around 13,400 to 13,800 and may be test 14,000 next month," he added.
Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities, said investors should take profits around current levels.
"The market may not be as strong over the next few days," he said.
The Hang Seng Index could meet "temporary resistance" around 13,700 to 13,800 points, said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
But he said after some consolidation, the index could gather enough momentum to test its all-time high.
"I think by June or July it will break through the level of 14,000 and try the 14,500 level," he said.
